mainTopic: A dying man's gift by spoken instruction, a גט ordered from a pit, a healthy man who says 'write a גט,' and choosing agents for a גט
overview: The amud opens by ruling that רבי אבינא may collect a gift left to him by a dying man, גניבא. The source is רב הונא's comparison: a dying man's גט is like his gift, so just as saying 'write' is enough for a גט, saying 'give' is enough for a gift without a קנין. רבי אבא objects, and the גמרא tries several explanations of what bothered him. In the end his problem is the odd wording 'from wine,' which the sages of ארץ ישראל explain was meant to strengthen the receiver's claim. A new משנה rules that people who hear a man in a pit ask for a גט for his wife may write it and give it. The גמרא answers the worry that the voice is a demon (a 'shadow of a shadow' was seen) and the worry that it is a rival wife (in a time of danger we write and give anyway). Another משנה says a healthy man who only says 'write a גט' is assumed to be teasing, unless his later actions prove he meant it, as in the story of the man who jumped from a roof. The amud ends with רבא ruling that a son can be appointed as an agent even when his father is present, and with the start of a new משנה about a husband who tells two people to give a גט.

steps.title: רבי אבינא can rely on his teacher רב הונא
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבינא may go collect the gift, based on רב הונא's rule that a dying man's גט is like his gift: if he recovers, both are cancelled.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let רבי אבינא pick up his basket and go to his teacher רב הונא. For רב הונא said: a man's גט is like his gift. If a dying man recovers, his gift is cancelled. So too, if he recovers, his גט is cancelled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says רבי אבינא can go collect the gift, and it brings רב הונא's comparison between a dying man's גט and his gift as the basis.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא treats a dying man's גט and his gift as one legal pattern. Here he uses the gift to teach about the גט: a gift given on a deathbed is cancelled if the giver gets well, so a deathbed גט is also cancelled if he gets well. This sets up the comparison that will be used in the other direction in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him lift his basket, meaning he may go and collect
His גט is like his gift
If he got up from his illness, it is cancelled

phrases.english: Let Rabbi Avina lift his basket
phrases.notes: A picture of going to collect what he was given: he can take his basket and fill it.

phrases.english: and go to Rav Huna his teacher –
as Rav Huna said:
His bill of divorce is like his gift,
just as with his gift, if he arose, he revokes it,
phrases.notes: 'Arose' means he recovered and got up from his sickbed.

phrases.english: so too his bill of divorce: if he arose, he revokes it.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּרָא רַבִּי אֲבִינָא לְסִילְּתֵיהּ, וַאֲזַל לְגַבֵּי דְּרַב הוּנָא רַבֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the ruling on the gift being discussed and starts to bring רב הונא as the source.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A dying man's גט and his gift are treated alike. If he recovers, both are cancelled.

steps.title: A spoken 'give' works for a gift just as a spoken 'write' works for a divorce
steps.stepSummary: The comparison also runs the other way. A dying man's גט works once he says 'write,' and his gift works once he says 'give,' with no קנין needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And just as with his גט, even if he did not spell it out, once he said 'write' it works even though he did not say 'give,' so too with his gift: once he said 'give,' it works even though nobody made a קנין from him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns רב הונא's comparison around. It uses the law of a dying man's גט to show that a dying man's spoken gift works with no formal act of acquiring.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the גט, saying only 'write' is enough. We understand that he also meant 'give' it to her. In the same way, for the gift, saying 'give' is enough even without a קנין. This is why רבי אבינא can collect.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Write!', the instruction to write the גט
'Give!', the instruction to hand it over
They made a קנין (a formal act of acquiring) from him

steps.whatToRemember: Through רב הונא's comparison, a dying man's spoken 'give' is enough to transfer a gift, just as his spoken 'write' is enough for a גט.

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה גִּיטּוֹ, אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא פָּרֵישׁ,
phrases.english: And just as with his bill of divorce, even though he did not specify,
once he said 'Write' –
even though he did not say 'Give' (it works);
phrases.notes: This points back to the משנה's case, where a dying man only said 'write a גט' and they write it and give it.

phrases.english: so too with his gift, once he said 'Give' –

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא קְנוֹ מִינֵּיהּ.
phrases.english: even though they did not acquire it from him (it works).

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמָה גִּיטּוֹ, אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא פָּרֵישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same comparison from step 1, now in the other direction, to support רבי אבינא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A dying man's gift works by his spoken instruction 'give,' even without a קנין.

steps.title: רבי אבא asks whether the comparison means a גט works after death
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא objects: if a גט is like a gift, then just as a gift works after death, a גט should also work after death.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא challenges this: if so, then just as a gift works after death, a גט should also work after death?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא attacks רב הונא's comparison by pushing it to a result that sounds wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A dying man's gift normally takes effect at his death. If the גט is truly like the gift in every way, it seems a גט should also work after death. That cannot be, so the comparison looks broken.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba objected to it:

phrases.aramaic: אִי – מָה מַתָּנָה יֶשְׁנָהּ לְאַחַר מִיתָה,
phrases.english: If so – just as a gift is valid after death,
so too a bill of divorce should be valid after death?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the comparison used in steps 1 and 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's comparison between a dying man's גט and his gift
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Carrying the comparison all the way through would mean a גט works after death, which seems wrong.

steps.title: That objection makes no sense
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects this version of רבי אבא's objection: everyone knows a גט cannot work after death.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can you compare them?! A gift works after death, fine. But is there such a thing as a גט after death?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says רבי אבא could not have meant that objection, because it is obviously not a real problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גט separates a living husband and wife. Once he dies the marriage is already over, so a גט after death makes no sense. Nobody would extend the comparison that far, so this cannot be what bothered רבי אבא.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not rejecting רב הונא here. It is rejecting one way of understanding רבי אבא's question. The next step tries a second explanation, which step 8 also rejects. רבי אבא's real question finally comes in step 9.

phrases.english: How can these be compared?!
Granted, a gift is valid after death,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא גֵּט – לְאַחַר מִיתָה מִי אִיכָּא?!
phrases.english: but a bill of divorce – is there one after death?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the version of רבי אבא's objection given in step 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the reading of רבי אבא's objection as being about a גט after death
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A גט after death is obviously meaningless, so nobody would extend the comparison that far.

steps.title: A second try at רבי אבא's objection: a partial gift needs a קנין
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא's real difficulty: this was a dying man's gift of only part of his property, and such a gift needs a קנין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is what was bothering רבי אבא: this is the gift of a dying man of only part of his property, and a dying man's gift of part of his property needs a קנין!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a new explanation of what bothered רבי אבא: this kind of gift should have needed a קנין. This explanation will itself be rejected in step 8.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שכיב מרע who gives away everything does not need a קנין. But if he gives only part, we suspect he expects to live, so it needs a קנין. Here he gave only part, so the spoken 'give' should not be enough.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who is dangerously ill, on his deathbed
Of only part of his property
It needs a formal act of acquiring

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא רַבִּי אַבָּא, הָכִי קָא קַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ:
phrases.english: Rather, this is what was difficult for Rabbi Abba:
It is the gift of a person on his deathbed of a portion of his property,

phrases.aramaic: וּמַתְּנַת שְׁכִיב מְרַע בְּמִקְצָת בָּעֲיָא קִנְיָן!
phrases.english: and the gift of a person on his deathbed of a portion requires an act of acquisition!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא רַבִּי אַבָּא, הָכִי קָא קַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected understanding of רבי אבא's objection with a second one, which step 8 will also reject.
steps.kashyaTarget: The conclusion in step 2 that the gift works without a קנין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This was a gift of only part of his property, and such a gift needs a קנין, so saying 'give' should not be enough.

steps.title: Does רב הונא really hold no קנין is needed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: does this mean רב הונא holds a partial gift needs no קנין? But the accepted law is that it does.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does that mean רב הונא holds it needs no קנין?! But we have an established rule that it needs a קנין!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sharpens רבי אבא's problem. Using רב הונא's rule here would put him against the accepted law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי אבינא collects based on רב הונא, it seems רב הונא thinks a partial deathbed gift needs no קנין. That goes against the settled rule. So either רב הונא disagrees with the accepted law, or something else is going on.

phrases.aramaic: מִכְּלָל דְּרַב הוּנָא סָבַר לָא בָּעֲיָא קִנְיָן?!
phrases.english: Does that imply that Rav Huna holds it does not require an act of acquisition?!
But we maintain that it does require an act of acquisition!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּלָל דְּרַב הוּנָא סָבַר לָא בָּעֲיָא קִנְיָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Develops רבי אבא's objection into a direct clash with the established law.
steps.kashyaTarget: Using רב הונא's rule to let רבי אבינא collect
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It would mean רב הונא holds a partial deathbed gift needs no קנין, which goes against the accepted law.

steps.title: Different here: an instruction given because of death
steps.stepSummary: This case is special. It was an instruction given because of approaching death (מצוה מחמת מיתה), so it works even without a קנין.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different here, because he was giving instructions on account of his death.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that this is not a regular partial gift. It is a dying man's final instruction, and that works without a קנין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A normal partial gift needs a קנין because he may expect to live. But when someone gives instructions because he knows he is dying, his words are carried out even for part of his property. So רב הונא does not go against the accepted law, and רבי אבינא may collect.

keyTerms.meaning: One who gives instructions because of approaching death

steps.whatToRemember: A partial gift by a שכיב מרע normally needs a קנין. But a מצוה מחמת מיתה, a final instruction given because of death, works by words alone.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the category of מתנת שכיב מרע has a special outcome when the gift is a final instruction because of death. The basic rule that a partial gift needs a קנין stays in place.

phrases.aramaic: שָׁאנֵי הָכָא דְּמְצַוֶּה מֵחֲמַת מִיתָה הוּא.
phrases.english: It is different here, since he is one who instructs on account of death.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection raised in steps 5 and 6.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: This looked like an ordinary partial deathbed gift, which needs a קנין.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is a מצוה מחמת מיתה, so it works without a קנין even for part of his property, and רב הונא agrees with the accepted law.

steps.title: Could רבי אבא really think this gift needs a קנין?
steps.stepSummary: Since the case was a מצוה מחמת מיתה, the גמרא asks how רבי אבא could have demanded a קנין, when everyone agrees such an instruction needs none.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this mean that רבי אבא holds that someone who gives instructions because he is about to die needs a קנין? But we hold that he does not need a קנין!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns back to רבי אבא. If the case was a deathbed instruction, his objection that a קנין is missing makes no sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 7 the גמרא said this was a מצוה מחמת מיתה, which works without a קנין. But then the version of רבי אבא's objection from step 5 falls apart, because the accepted law is that such an instruction needs no קנין. So the גמרא needs a new explanation of what bothered רבי אבא.

keyTerms.meaning: By implication: what follows from what was just said
Someone who gives instructions because he expects to die soon
We hold / it is the accepted law

phrases.english: Does this mean, by implication, that רבי אבא holds:
one who gives instructions because of approaching death needs a קנין?!
But we hold
that he does not need a קנין!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the answer of step 7 to undermine the version of רבי אבא's objection given in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The step 5 version of רבי אבא's objection (that a קנין was needed).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the case is a deathbed instruction, and the law is that such an instruction needs no קנין, רבי אבא could not have objected that a קנין was missing.

steps.title: רבי אבא's real problem: the wording 'from wine'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says רבי אבא's actual difficulty was the odd wording: not 'wine,' not 'the value of wine,' but 'from wine.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is what was difficult for רבי אבא: He did not say 'wine.' He did not say 'the value of wine.' He said 'from wine'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new version of what bothered רבי אבא. It was the strange wording of the gift.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dying man (גניבא) said to give 400 זוז 'from wine.' If he meant wine itself, he should have said 'wine.' If he meant money, he should have said 'the value of wine.' Saying 'from wine' is unclear, and that is what bothered רבי אבא.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather: drops the earlier explanation and gives a new one
This is what was difficult for him

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא רַבִּי אַבָּא, הָכִי קָא קַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ:
phrases.english: Rather, this is what was difficult for רבי אבא:
He did not say "wine,"
phrases.notes: "He" is the dying man, גניבא, who gave 400 זוז to רבי אבינא.

phrases.english: he did not say "the value of wine,"
he said "from wine"!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא רַבִּי אַבָּא, הָכִי קָא קַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 8 by replacing the earlier version of רבי אבא's objection with a new one about wording.
steps.kashyaTarget: The meaning of the dying man's wording 'from wine.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The phrase 'from wine' is neither 'wine' nor 'the value of wine,' so it is unclear what the man meant to give.

steps.title: רבי זירא: 'from wine' strengthens the gift
steps.stepSummary: The other אמורא, who was not bothered, explains that 'from wine' was said to strengthen the receiver's claim.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one: 'from wine' was said to strengthen his position.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי זירא had no problem with the wording 'from wine.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: By naming the wine as the source of payment, the dying man made it easier for רבי אבינא to collect. The heirs cannot push him off, because a clear source for the 400 זוז has been marked. So the wording is not confusing; it is protective.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one: the other side of the disagreement
To strengthen his position / make his claim stronger

phrases.english: And the other one holds: "from wine" was said
phrases.notes: "The other one" is רבי זירא, who was not bothered by this case.

phrases.english: in order to strengthen his position.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording problem raised in step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the wording as purposeful rather than unclear.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'From wine' seems vague: is the gift wine or money?
steps.terutzMaskana: 'From wine' names a source of payment so the receiver can collect more easily.

steps.title: ארץ ישראל confirms רבי זירא's reading
steps.stepSummary: A message from ארץ ישראל says the same thing: 'from wine' was to strengthen the receiver's position.
steps.simpleTranslation: They sent from there: 'from wine' was said to strengthen his position.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for רבי זירא's explanation from a message sent from ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sages of ארץ ישראל explained the wording exactly as רבי זירא did. This backs up his view and closes the discussion of גניבא's gift.

keyTerms.meaning: They sent from there: a message from the sages of ארץ ישראל

steps.whatToRemember: A deathbed instruction (מצוה מחמת מיתה) works without a קנין. The words 'from wine' were not confusing; they named a source so the receiver could collect more easily.

phrases.english: They sent from there:
"from wine" was said in order to strengthen his position.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the explanation given in step 10.
steps.raayaObject: רבי זירא's explanation that 'from wine' strengthens the gift.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A message from the sages of ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: משנה: a man in a pit orders a גט
steps.stepSummary: A man thrown into a pit says anyone who hears his voice should write a גט for his wife; those who hear him should write it and give it.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Someone who was thrown into a pit and said, 'Anyone who hears my voice should write a גט for my wife,' those people should write it and give it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It says that people who only hear a man's voice from a pit may write and deliver a גט for his wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the people writing a גט know who the husband is. Here they only hear a voice, yet the משנה still lets them write and give the גט. This sets up the גמרא's question about how they can trust a voice alone.

phrases.english: משנה:
Someone who was thrown into a pit,
and he said: anyone who hears his voice
should write a גט for his wife,
these people should write it and give it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic with a new משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: People who hear a man in a pit ask for a גט for his wife may write and deliver it.

steps.title: Maybe the voice is a demon
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: since no one sees the man, maybe the voice belongs to a demon.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: But let us worry that maybe it is a demon!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה. If people only hear a voice, how do they know it is really a person?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lets people act on a voice alone. The גמרא worries the voice could be a שד pretending to be the husband, and then the גט would be worthless.

phrases.english: גמרא:
But let us worry that maybe it is a demon!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of the משנה in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that people may act on a voice from a pit.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A voice alone does not prove a human is speaking; it might be a demon.

steps.title: רב יהודה: they saw a human form
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה answers that the משנה speaks of a case where they saw the figure in the pit looked like a person.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: It is a case where they saw that he had the form of a person.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers the demon worry by narrowing the case of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה is not about a voice alone. The people saw a human shape in the pit, so there is no reason to fear a demon.

phrases.english: רב יהודה said:
It is when they saw that he had the form of a person.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the case of the משנה to a specific situation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seems to rely on a voice alone, which could be a demon.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה speaks of a case where they saw a human form, so there is no demon worry.

steps.title: Demons can look human too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב יהודה's answer: שדים can also take on a human form.
steps.simpleTranslation: Demons too can make themselves look like people!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the last answer. Seeing a human-looking figure in the pit does not prove it is a person, because שדים can also look like people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה said the משנה is talking about a case where they saw a human-looking figure. The גמרא says that is not enough proof, since a שד can disguise itself as a person.

keyTerms.meaning: They really can take on a likeness (look like something)

phrases.english: They too can really take on a human likeness!
phrases.notes: 'They' means the שדים mentioned in the question just before this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of רב יהודה in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that seeing a human shape proves it is a person
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שדים can look human, so a human appearance proves nothing.

steps.title: They saw that he casts a shadow
steps.stepSummary: The case is where they saw that the figure has a shadow.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a case where they saw that he has a shadow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by adding a further sign. The figure in the pit was seen casting a shadow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that a real body casts a shadow, while a שד might not. So the shadow is offered as stronger proof than just the human look.

phrases.english: Where they saw that he has a shadow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15 by narrowing the case further.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A human look alone might be a שד.
steps.terutzMaskana: The case is where a shadow was also seen.

steps.title: Demons have shadows too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges again: שדים also have a shadow.
steps.simpleTranslation: Demons also have a shadow!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the shadow proof. שדים can also cast a shadow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The shadow sign does not separate a person from a שד, so the case is still not proven to be a real man.

phrases.english: They too have a shadow!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The shadow as proof of a human
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שדים also cast shadows, so the sign does not help.

steps.title: They saw a shadow of a shadow
steps.stepSummary: The case is where they saw the figure has a 'shadow of a shadow.'
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a case where they saw that he has the shadow of a shadow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with an even more specific sign: a 'shadow of a shadow.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since a plain shadow is not enough, the גמרא raises the bar to a second-level shadow, which it assumes only a real person has.

keyTerms.meaning: A shadow of a shadow (a second, fainter shadow)

phrases.english: Where they saw that he has a shadow of a shadow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 17 by narrowing the case one more level.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A single shadow could belong to a שד.
steps.terutzMaskana: The case is where a shadow of a shadow was seen.

steps.title: Maybe demons have that too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: perhaps שדים also have a shadow of a shadow.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe they too have a shadow of a shadow?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges once more, asking how we know שדים do not also have a shadow of a shadow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time the challenge is not a known fact but a doubt. The גמרא needs a source showing that this sign really is unique to humans.

phrases.english: But perhaps they too have it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 18.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: No proof has been given that שדים lack a shadow of a shadow.

steps.title: Demons have no shadow of a shadow
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא reports that his son יונתן taught him that שדים have a shadow but not a shadow of a shadow.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא said: My son יונתן taught me that demons have a shadow, but they do not have a shadow of a shadow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the question with a tradition from רבי חנינא. שדים have a shadow but never a shadow of a shadow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This confirms that a shadow of a shadow is a sure sign of a real person. So when the משנה says to write and give the גט, it is talking about a case where this sign was seen.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who reports this teaching

steps.whatToRemember: The final sign that the voice in the pit is a real person: a shadow of a shadow, which שדים do not have.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥanina said:
Yonatan my son taught me:
They have a shadow,
but they do not have a shadow of a shadow.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא: לִימְּדַנִי יוֹנָתָן בְּנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the doubt of step 19 with a received tradition.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe שדים have every kind of shadow.
steps.terutzMaskana: שדים have a shadow but not a shadow of a shadow, so that sign proves a human.

steps.title: Maybe the voice is a rival wife
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: perhaps the voice belongs to the woman's צרה (co-wife) trying to trick her.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps it is a rival wife!
steps.whatsHappening: Now that we know it is a human, the גמרא raises a new worry: maybe the voice is not the husband but his other wife, who wants to cause trouble.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if the voice is human, we still do not know it is the husband. A jealous צרה could fake a divorce so her rival thinks she is free to remarry, which would leave her forbidden to both men.

keyTerms.meaning: A co-wife, the husband's other wife (often a rival)

phrases.english: But perhaps it is a rival wife!
phrases.notes: She would be faking the husband's voice to trick the other wife into a fake divorce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After proving the voice is human, it questions whether it is really the husband.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule in the משנה (step 12) to write and give the גט
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A human voice could still be a rival wife pretending to be the husband.

steps.title: In a time of danger we write and give anyway
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא from the school of רבי ישמעאל teaches that in danger, a גט is written and given even without recognizing the man.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in the school of רבי ישמעאל: In a time of danger, one writes and gives a גט even though they do not recognize the man.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא. When there is danger, we write and give the גט even if we cannot be sure who is speaking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חז"ל were lenient here so the wife would not become an עגונה, stuck unable to remarry. So the small worry of a rival wife is not enough to hold back the גט.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in the school of רבי ישמעאל (a ברייתא)

steps.whatToRemember: In a time of danger, a גט is written and given even when the sender cannot be identified.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that in emergencies the הלכה relaxes its normal checks so a woman will not be left an עגונה.

phrases.english: A Sage from the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
In a time of danger,
they write and give a bill of divorce
even though they do not recognize him.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל: בִּשְׁעַת הַסַּכָּנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the rival-wife worry of step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Citing a ברייתא with a leniency for emergencies
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any doubt about who is speaking should stop the גט.
steps.terutzMaskana: In danger, we write and give even without recognizing the speaker.

steps.title: A healthy man who only says 'write a גט'
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה rules that a healthy man who says 'Write a גט for my wife' was likely just teasing her.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A healthy man who said, 'Write a גט for my wife,' wanted to tease her.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. If a healthy man only says 'write a גט' and not 'give it,' we assume he was just teasing, so the גט is not valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the man in the pit or someone very sick, a healthy man is in no rush. Since he said only to write it and not to give it, we do not assume he really meant to divorce.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean a healthy man can never give a גט by telling others. The problem is only that he said 'write' without saying 'give.'

phrases.english: MISHNA:
A healthy man who said: 'Write a bill of divorce for my wife'
wanted to tease her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה, moving from the danger case of the pit to a healthy man.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A healthy man who only says 'write a גט' is assumed to be teasing, and the גט is not valid.

steps.title: The man who fell from the roof
steps.stepSummary: A story: a healthy man said 'write a גט,' then fell from a roof and died. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל rules it depends on how he fell.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a story about a healthy man who said, 'Write a גט for my wife,' then went up to the roof, fell, and died. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said: If he fell on his own, it is a valid גט. If the wind pushed him, it is not a גט.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה tells a story about a healthy man who said 'write a גט' and then died falling from a roof. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל rules based on whether he jumped or was blown off.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he jumped on purpose, he knew he was about to die, so his 'write a גט' was meant seriously and the גט is valid. If the wind knocked him off, he was just a healthy man who was teasing, so the basic rule of the משנה applies and it is not a גט.

keyTerms.meaning: He fell on his own (on purpose)
A תנא who rules on this case

steps.whatToRemember: A healthy man's 'write a גט' counts only if he clearly knew he was about to die, as when he jumped on purpose.

phrases.english: There was an incident with a healthy man who said:
'Write a bill of divorce for my wife,'
and he went up to the top of the roof, fell, and died;
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said:

phrases.aramaic: אִם מֵעַצְמוֹ נָפַל, הֲרֵי זֶה גֵּט,
phrases.english: If he fell on his own, it is a valid bill of divorce,
phrases.notes: He means the man jumped on purpose, so he knew he was going to die.

phrases.english: if the wind pushed him, it is not a bill of divorce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the rule of step 23 in a real case and when it changes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the healthy man jumped on purpose, the גט is valid. If the wind pushed him, it is not.

steps.title: Why bring a story that contradicts the rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה cites a story that seems to go against its own rule about a healthy man.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Does the משנה bring a story to contradict itself?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is surprised. The משנה said a healthy man who says 'write a גט' was only teasing, but then it tells a story where such a גט can be valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a story in a משנה supports the rule just stated. Here the story shows a case where a healthy man's 'write a גט' does count, so it seems to clash with the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: An incident, a story that happened

phrases.english: GEMARA
An incident to contradict?!
phrases.notes: The story is supposed to back up the rule, but here it seems to go against it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the relationship between the משנה's rule (step 23) and its story (step 24).
steps.kashyaTarget: The structure of the משנה: rule followed by an apparently opposite story.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule says a healthy man's 'write a גט' means nothing, yet the story shows a case where it is a valid גט.

steps.title: The משנה is missing a line
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא fills in a missing line: if his later actions prove he was serious, it is a valid גט, and the story illustrates exactly that.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה is missing words, and this is what it teaches: If his end proves his beginning, it is a valid גט. And there was also a story with a healthy man who said, 'Write a גט for my wife,' then went up to the roof, fell, and died. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said: If he fell on his own, it is a valid גט. If the wind pushed him, it is not a גט.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה left out a line. With that line added, the story no longer contradicts the rule. It is an example of the added line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a healthy man is assumed to be teasing. But if what he does afterward shows he meant it, like jumping off a roof on purpose, the גט is valid. If the wind pushed him, his death was an accident and says nothing about what he meant, so the teasing assumption stays.

keyTerms.meaning: The text is missing something; words must be filled in
And this is what it teaches
His end proves his beginning: later actions reveal what he meant at first

steps.whatToRemember: A healthy man's 'write a גט' is normally treated as teasing, unless his later actions prove he meant it.

phrases.english: It is missing words,
and this is what it teaches:
If his end proves his beginning,
phrases.notes: What he did at the end shows he was serious when he first spoke.

phrases.english: it is a valid גט;
and there was also an incident with a healthy man who said:
"Write a גט for my wife,"
and he went up to the roof, fell, and died.
And רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said:

phrases.aramaic: אִם מֵעַצְמוֹ נָפַל – הֲרֵי זֶה גֵּט,
phrases.english: If he fell on his own, it is a valid גט;
if the wind pushed him, it is not a גט.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 25 by adding a missing clause to the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Filling in missing words in the משנה (חסורי מיחסרא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The story seemed to contradict the rule that a healthy man was only teasing.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה includes an exception: when later actions prove he meant it, the גט is valid. The story illustrates that exception.

steps.title: The man in the synagogue and the teacher who died
steps.stepSummary: A man told a teacher, his son, and another man that 'two of you' should write a גט for his wife, and then the teacher died.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain man entered the synagogue and found a children's teacher and his son sitting there, and another person sitting with them. He said to them: Two of you should write a גט for my wife. In the end, the teacher died.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a new story. It is setting up a question about who the man meant by 'two of you.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: A father and son are relatives, so they cannot act together as the two people for the גט. So the man must have meant either the teacher with the other man, or the son with the other man. Now that the teacher has died, that difference matters.

phrases.english: A certain man who entered the synagogue
found a children's teacher and his son sitting there,
and another person was sitting with them.
He said to them:
Two of you
should write a גט for my wife.
In the end, the teacher died.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new case about appointing agents for a גט.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Case setup: 'two of you' was said to a father, his son, and a third man, and the father died.

steps.title: Would people choose the son when the father is there?
steps.stepSummary: The question: when the father is present, do people pick the son as their agent, or not?
steps.simpleTranslation: Do people make a son their agent when the father is there, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the man most likely meant by 'two of you.' Could he have meant the son, or only the father?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If people do sometimes choose the son even with the father present, the son and the other man may count as the agents and can still write the גט. If people would never pick the son over the father, then the man meant the teacher, and with the teacher dead the agency is gone.

keyTerms.meaning: In the father's presence, when the father is also there

phrases.english: Do people make
a son an agent where the father is present,
or not?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי מְשַׁוּוּ אִינָשֵׁי בְּרָא שְׁלִיחָא בִּמְקוֹם אַבָּא, אוֹ לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks the question that the story in step 27 sets up.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the man could have meant the son (with the third man) as his agents, given that the father was present.

steps.title: רב נחמן: people don't choose the son
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says people do not appoint the son when the father is there.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: People do not make a son an agent where the father is present.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers no. The man must have meant the father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the man meant the teacher and the other man, the teacher's death ends the plan. The son cannot step in to write the גט.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who answers the question here

phrases.english: רב נחמן said:
People do not make
a son an agent where the father is present;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question of step 28.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No. The man meant the father, so the son and the other man cannot write the גט.

steps.title: רב פפי: people do choose the son
steps.stepSummary: רב פפי disagrees: people do appoint the son even when the father is there.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב פפי said: People do make a son an agent where the father is present.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפי gives the opposite answer. The man could have meant the son.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the son is a possible choice, then the son and the other man still count as the 'two of you.' They can write the גט even though the teacher died.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who disagrees with רב נחמן

phrases.english: And רב פפי said:
People do make
a son an agent where the father is present.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite answer to רב נחמן's in step 29.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes. The son can be the agent, so he and the other man may write the גט.

steps.title: רבא rules like רב פפי
steps.stepSummary: רבא decides the הלכה: people do appoint the son even with the father present.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The הלכה is that people do make a son an agent where the father is present.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא settles the argument and rules like רב פפי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In practice, the son and the other man may write the גט after the teacher died. רב נחמן's view is not followed here.

keyTerms.meaning: The אמורא who decides the dispute

steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה follows רבא: a son can be the intended agent even when his father is present. So the son and the third man can write the גט.

phrases.english: רבא said: The הלכה is:
People do make
a son an agent where the father is present.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides between רב נחמן (step 29) and רב פפי (step 30).
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows רב פפי: the son can serve as agent with the third man, so the גט may be written.

steps.title: New משנה: A husband tells two people to give a divorce document to his wife
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה opens with a case: a husband says to two people, 'Give a גט to my wife.'
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If a man said to two people, 'Give a גט to my wife,'
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts here, and it opens by describing a case. This line only sets up the situation, so the ruling about what the two people may do comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Notice the exact wording: the husband speaks to two people, and his instruction is only to 'give' the גט. He does not say anything about writing it. That exact wording is the starting point for the case, so hold onto it while reading the rest of the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה. The text marks the start of a new משנה.
Give (said to more than one person).

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a continuation of the story about the teacher who died. It is a brand-new משנה. Also, the sentence is not finished yet; the ruling comes next.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
If a man said to two people:
'Give a divorce document to my wife,'

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: None; this is a plain opening of a new משנה.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the earlier case. After רבא's ruling in step 31, the text turns to a new משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling is given yet. The line only describes the case: a husband says to two people, 'Give a גט to my wife.' The ruling follows in the next part of the משנה.
